title: Pilot asymmetric ingress/egress pricing with streaming credit caps and soft-commit guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and run a 6-week pilot that charges distinct ingress (input) and egress (output) token rates, introduces a streaming egress credit to encourage low-latency responses, and implements a soft minimum monthly commit guardrail for small/PLG accounts. Goal is to validate unit economics, surface customer acceptance, and flag contract/security implications for enterprise accounts.
hypothesis: Asymmetric IO pricing (lower ingress rate, higher egress rate) plus a modest streaming egress credit will reduce unit cost for retrieval-heavy apps while preserving revenue from generation-heavy apps; a soft minimum commit ($X/month) prevents pathological under-usage for reserved stack while remaining acceptable to small customers if communicated as optional/waivable.
success_metrics: Reduce average egress-cost-per-output-token for retrieval-heavy PLG cohort by >=10%
Net revenue delta across pilot cohorts within ±2% over 8 weeks
No more than 1% increase in billing disputes for pilot cohorts
Accuracy of cost estimator in Console within ±5% for pilot traffic
experimental_setup: Two-arm rollout: Control = current symmetric per-token rates; Treatment = asymmetric rates + streaming credit + optional soft commit. Sample size: ~1,200 orgs (800 PLG small, 300 mid-market, 100 enterprise opt-ins). Duration: 6 weeks of live billing telemetry plus 2 weeks of shadow simulation. Instrumentation: per-request IO tags, streaming flag, session lengths, and metered tokens stored in billing-v2. Billing system will run simulated invoices for the shadow period to detect rounding/aggregation issues.
pricing_proposals: Variant Alpha (conservative): ingress $0.50 / 1M tokens, egress $1.50 / 1M tokens, streaming egress credit 15% on egress portion, soft commit floor $25/mo (opt-in waiver for startups)
Variant Beta (balanced): ingress $0.40 / 1M tokens, egress $1.80 / 1M tokens, streaming egress credit 20%, soft commit floor $50/mo with 30-day forgiveness window

Variant Gamma (aggressive): ingress $0.30 / 1M tokens, egress $2.10 / 1M tokens, streaming egress credit 30% but capped to first 200K streaming tokens per org/month, soft commit floor $100/mo (targeted at mid-market)
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize pricing variant (Feb week 3). 2) Legal & Security review (shadow only). 3) Engineering to enable shadow billing and tagging in billing-v2 (2 sprints). 4) Internal shadow run with simulated invoices (2 weeks). 5) Opt-in beta for 100 orgs (2 weeks). 6) Expand to full treatment cohort (6 weeks) with live invoices and close monitoring. 7) Post-pilot review and decision. Billing UI will show per-org "pilot" banner and cost estimator.
gating_criteria: Billing engine completes simulated invoices with <0.1% mismatch vs expected aggregation
Legal accepts contract language for commit floor and opt-out mechanics
No significant customer support spike (>15% above baseline) during opt-in beta
Telemetry shows expected cost patterns for at least two archetypes (chat-heavy, retrieval-heavy)

notes_for_sales: Key talking points: 1) Asymmetric rates are easier to reason about for retrieval-first apps — lower ingress cost. 2) Streaming credit reduces egress cost for low-latency sessions and is capped per plan for fairness. 3) Soft commit is optional and can be waived for qualifying startups; enterprise contracts can negotiate floors and rollover terms. Provide link to pilot spec and cost estimator in pitch pack.
simulation_summary: Finance simulations across 4 archetypes indicate: retrieval-heavy (R) sees ~12% lower token spend under Beta; chat/generation-heavy (G) sees ~8% higher spend but higher ARPU; mixed (M) cohort breaks even. Sensitivity analysis shows capping streaming credits prevents 20% of edge cases where cost delta >30%.
